Z-drug hypnotics: 2

A patient taking zolpidem is found cooking overnight and has no memory of the event. The behavior occurred while not fully awake. Which serious adverse effect should prompt stopping the drug and contacting the prescriber?

  1. Additive CNS and respiratory depression
  2. Dangerous sedative withdrawal
  3. Complex sleep behavior
  4. Additive sedation and impaired alertness
  5. Residual next-day impairment
Answer and explanation

Complex sleep behavior

Sleepwalking, sleep-driving or other activities without full awareness can occur with Z-drugs and require discontinuation and clinical review.

Option explanations

Complex sleep behavior: Sleepwalking, sleep-driving or other activities without full awareness can occur with Z-drugs and require discontinuation and clinical review.

Additive sedation and impaired alertness: Combining melatonin with other sedating substances can increase drowsiness and impairment; review all medicines and alcohol exposure. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Residual next-day impairment: Sedative effects may persist after awakening and impair driving even when the patient feels awake. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Additive CNS and respiratory depression: Combining sedatives with opioids or alcohol increases risk of profound sedation and respiratory depression. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Dangerous sedative withdrawal: Abrupt cessation after dependence can cause severe anxiety, autonomic symptoms and seizures; an individualized taper may be needed. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
